# Solid-State Residual Value Impact

- Document Class: Hypothesis
- Status: Active
- Date: 2026-05-10
- Category: EV residual value
- Scope: Potential impact of semi-solid and all-solid-state batteries on older EV values.
- Sources: `raw/research/2026-05-10-ev-battery-technologies/sources/06-semi-solid-quasi-solid-batteries.md`; `raw/research/2026-05-10-ev-battery-technologies/sources/07-all-solid-state-lithium-metal.md`
- Related: `wiki/references/semi-solid-quasi-solid-batteries.reference.md`; `wiki/references/all-solid-state-lithium-metal-batteries.reference.md`

## Hypothesis

Solid-state battery announcements will affect buyer expectations before they materially affect mainstream used-EV prices. Real residual-value impact requires high-volume vehicles with verified range, charging, safety, cost, and warranty advantages.

## Rationale

IEA characterizes solid-state as large pilot stage. Toyota, BMW, QuantumScape, Stellantis, and Factorial show credible progress, but early products are expected to be limited or demonstrator-scale. Semi-solid or quasi-solid systems may appear first, creating terminology confusion.

## Key Risk

If an OEM reaches affordable high-volume solid-state production earlier than expected, older lithium-ion EVs could face faster technology-obsolescence discounts.
